newsitem.title: UK: AfDB says eyes rand, dollar and mark Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: AfDB says eyes rand, dollar and mark Eurobonds.

text.p: The African Development Bank (AfDB) plans to raise up to another $450 million on the international capital markets in 1997, its treasurer told Reuters on Wednesday.
It will issue a rand Eurobond for up to 150 million rand ($33 million), and the rest will be raised via dollar and/or mark transactions, he said.
"We have a requirement for $400 to $450 million," Thierry de Longuemar, AfDB treasurer, said.
"We plan to tap the rand market and we are also considering an issue in dollars and/or marks. These will be done in the fourth quarter of 1997."
De Longuemar said the AfDB was considering launching a deal which would be exchangeable into the euro when the single currency was introduced.
"For the time being our funding needs are rather limited to yen and dollars. (But) we are considering the possibility, especially if we do tap the mark market."

He said it was too early to decide the maturity of the rand bond, which would be for 100 to 150 million rand. In February the AfDB launched a 100 million rand two-year bond which paid a 15 percent coupon.

On Wednesday the AfDB raised 30 billion yen via a five-year subordinated bond, which paid 22 basis points over Japanese government bonds. De Longuemar said the deal would be used to refinance a maturing yen bond.
"We expect the transaction to be fully sold over the coming few days," he said, adding sales were made to a mixture of European and Asian fund managers and private client networks.

"The overall lack of current coupon yen bonds and the pick-up in yield this transaction offers (over government bonds) gives us confidence in the transaction," he said. ($ = 4.561 South African Rand) -- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
